title: Implement Configurable Sync Behavior with Keyboard Shortcut
description: The FlowFrame Productivity Studio currently has a hardcoded synchronization service that runs on startup. This task requires modifying the application to introduce a user-configurable sync behavior. The user should be able to choose whether sync runs automatically on startup or only when triggered manually. This new functionality needs to be driven by a setting in `app_config.json` and the manual trigger should be accessible via a keyboard shortcut.

project_spec.name: FlowFrame Productivity Studio
project_spec.description:
FlowFrame Productivity Studio is a cross-platform desktop media organizer and quick-action hub designed for creatives and knowledge workers who frequently juggle screenshots, screen recordings, and reference clips. The application lets users instantly capture, tag, and arrange rich media assets into project-oriented "frames" with powerful keyboard shortcuts, intuitive drag-and-drop, and a fluid MVVM-driven GUI. Core productivity boosters such as lightning-fast search, one-keystroke snippet insertion, and customizable workflow plug-ins turn scattered media into an always-ready knowledge base.

A lightweight C client handles the responsive interface, file management, and local caching, while serverless back-end functions (AWS Lambda or Azure Functions) perform compute-intensive jobs—thumbnail generation, format transcoding, OCR, smart tagging, and encrypted backup—on demand. This separation keeps the desktop app snappy and offline-capable, yet instantly scalable whenever users trigger heavy tasks. Real-time updates, auto-sync, and live collaboration events flow through an event-driven observer layer that propagates state changes to the view models and optional plug-ins, ensuring zero-friction productivity across devices.
dependencies: SDL2 (cross-platform windowing, input, and accelerated 2D graphics)
libui or Gtk-4 (native-looking GUI toolkit with drag-and-drop support)
libcurl (secure HTTPS calls to serverless REST / GraphQL endpoints)
jansson or json-c (fast JSON parsing for payloads to/from Lambda)
SQLite + SQLCipher (encrypted local cache and user preferences)
libzip (packaging media bundles for offline use and auto-updates)
cURLpp or custom updater shell for delta auto-update retrieval
OpenSSL (TLS, cryptographic functions for secure token storage)
Plugin SDK headers (dlopen/LoadLibrary wrappers for plug-in loading)
CMake (multi-platform build and easy CI/CD integration)
